sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that as per prosecution story, victim is a 15 years old girl with less developed mind.
According to her mother, she does not talk much and speaks only their local tribal language i.e. Gondi.
On 15/11/2020 complainant had gone to fields to give food to her husband at about 7.00 p.m.
When at 9.00 p.m. she returned back, then she did not find the victim at home.
Thereafter she found victim in the Badi of her house where she was standing under a Mahua tree on the Medh of appellant-Mantu.

When she asked the victim as to who brought her,
then she informed that Mantu had brought her.
Mantu started running.

Thereafter when this complainant observed that there was enlargement of stomach of the victim, she asked for the reason, then it was informed that at the time of Ganesh festival on 22/08/2020, Mantu had violated her privacy and on 15/11/2020 also Mantu had violated her privacy.

3. It is submitted that contrary to this oral testimony, scientific evidence is available on record as Ex.P/25 which reveals that Mantu is not a NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16253 3 CRA-740-2025 biological father of the newborn child to whom victim had given birth.
Thus, it is submitted the appellant has been falsely implicated.
Scientific evidence clearly defies the prosecution's version, therefore, prayer is made to record a finding of acquittal.

4. Shri Veer Vikrant Singh, learned Dy. Advocate General, in his turn, supports the impugned judgment and submits that victim was a minor at the time of incident, therefore, nothing more is required to be read into it.
5. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.

Mother of the victim (PW-1)
deposed that Mantu is her neighbourer.
In relationship, he is uncle of this witness.
This witness admitted dispute with Mantu aged about 50 years on account of agricultural operations so also in regard to boundaries of agricultural holdings.
6. P.W.-5 did not support the prosecution case.
This witness was declared hostile.
When leading questions were put to her, this witness deposed that the child born out of her womb, is that of Mantu, however, this is contrary to the DNA report (Ex.P/25).
When these facts are taken into consideration, then it is evident that scientific evidence does not corroborate the oral testimony of the witnesses.
P.W.-5 also admitted that she does not understand Hindi.
This witness admitted that the questions which were put by the learned counsel in cross-examination in Hindi, have been, in fact, answered by her as per the signs/signals made by her mother.

That means testimony of P.W.-5 is not independent testimony especially when it is not mentioned in the the testimony by the learned trial Court that any interpreter was called for to interpret and translate the questions put either by the Court NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:16253 4 CRA-740-2025 or by the counsel in Hindi in Gondi language which is understood by the victim as per admission of her mother and mother was an interested witness.
This is a serious lapse on the part of the concerned trial Court.
It has also come on record and admitted by the mother of the victim (PW-1) that there was enmity with Mantu.
Father of the victim (PW-2) has also deposed on the same line.
7. Enmity is a double edged sword.

Oral testimony is usually given precedence over any other evidence, but, when there is oral evidence in regard to a sensitive matter like violation of privacy and when there is a scientific evidence which has remained unrebutted and unchallenged in the form of Mantu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 25 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/169386052/
2 DNA report, categorically mentioning that child born out of the womb of the victim is not biologically fathered by the accused/appellant, then as per the judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Balaram Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh, 2023 SCC OnLine SC 1468, wherein in para- 18 it is held that as already discussed herein above, previous enmity is a double edged weapon; on the one hand it provides the motive, whereas on the other hand, the possibility of false implication cannot be ruled out, we are of the opinion that when motive is clear from the evidence of P.W.-1 and P.W.-2 about the enmity, and when scientific evidence is contrary to the oral evidence and it has not been challenged, then the conviction only on the basis of oral evidence and that too is not corroborated and tainted with elements of enmity, cannot be given precedence over the scientific evidence, thus, accordingly, in view of the scientific evidence available on record, impugned judgment cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.
